candidates.classification: conditional source-derived post-write containment change after bulk repair suppresses a per-item error; supported state and transaction outcome not observed
candidates.detail: The current batch loop increments success only for submit(...).is_ok(), discards every error and returns Ok when any item succeeds. For a nested repairable item, detach_if_nested deletes its containment edge before merge_empty_container can fail. Assume an otherwise admissible parent becomes empty, is not itself nested and has a unique valid personal backing row of quantity one; neither parent nor an eligible same-item target stack has an ItemCondition, and the target has no physical object and quantity u32::MAX. Assume another repair item in the same batch succeeds. The parent merge reaches checked_add and returns a stack overflow after the edge deletion; submit propagates that error, the batch ignores it and returns Ok because of the other success. Pinned SpacetimeDB source documentation says successful reducers commit, so source predicts the failed item’s removed containment edge survives without a repair order. No product code, reducer or database was run.

Expected ineligible or undamaged items may intentionally be skipped; individual submission propagates the error. The example assumes specific valid backing, parent/target stack, successful peer, and no later transaction failure. Reachability of that stack state and actual deployed transaction behavior remain unproved. Other post-write refresh errors are connected but no concrete supported cause is claimed.
